Containment actions (firewall block, host quarantine, AV scan) were attempted but denied due to policy or parameter errors.

arguments.summary: Critical data exfiltration incident involving unauthorized upload of 2.3 GB of PCI, PII, and financial data from Finance shared drive to a personal Dropbox account. User j.martinez compressed 847 sensitive files using encrypted 7z format. DLP system detected content patterns and triggered alert. Investigation revealed no malware presence but highlighted gaps in monitoring encrypted file creation and cloud uploads. No containment actions were approved during the Admin phase.

timeline.description: Suspicious network scan activity detected from IP 10.0.2.15 (unrelated asset); logged but not linked to user j.martinez.
Normal authentication event on IT workstation; no direct connection to incident.
DLP system triggers alert: large-scale upload of encrypted archives containing PCI and PII data from WS-FIN-AP01 (10.0.10.51) to personal Dropbox account j.martinez.personal@gmail.com.
SIEM queries confirm repeated use of 7z.exe and POST requests to dropbox.com from source IP 10.0.10.51 within the past 24 hours.

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration attempt was detected and blocked on SRV-SQL-PROD-01. The service account 'svc-sql-prod' was misused to dump 4.2 million customer records via mysqldump. Forensic analysis revealed initial compromise via a spear-phishing email to user jsmith on WS-FIN-042, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. Lateral movement to the SQL server occurred via SMB. Exfiltration via SCP to 203.0.113.88 was blocked by the firewall. The root cause was an unpatched endpoint and excessive privileges for the service account.
